checks.Title: Seduce, don't just observe
checks.Evidence: The aerobloc passage seduces before any horror lands: 'A city block... held aloft on an eigenlift frame so wide she had to work to find its edges in the murk,' followed by her palm on the glass and the physical joy of reverse-engineering it — 'Something settled in behind her sternum, warm and level and entirely uninvited' — and the terminal's Hyper Reality noise, the AIs that 'talk to her,' and the lived-in wrongness of jury-rigged ductwork ('Nobody had redrawn any of it since the day it first went in, and she liked it the better for that') all build allure through texture before the extortion plot's menace takes over.

checks.Title: Open with the world doing its work
checks.Evidence: The story opens directly with heist tension already engaged ('The job was going beautifully. That was always when you had to watch it.') and plunges into active infiltration, drones, and counter-intrusion alarms within the first paragraphs — there is no grounded commute/transaction beat where a jaded local simply moves through the world before the plot demands attention.
checks.Fix: Precede the heist with a short, low-stakes beat of the protagonist doing something mundane in her world (paying for something, riding transit, reading a machine's hum) so the reader falls into the setting before the crisis begins.

checks.Title: Gloss first mentions in-voice, never dump
checks.Evidence: Terms like 'neuretics' (used immediately for embodied action: 'Her neuretics ran a direct line into the building's maintenance scheduler') and 'Husk' are glossed lightly through function, but 'CorpoNations' and 'Φ' currency and 'GLMZ'/'The Low'/'Seam margin' are dropped in with only partial orientation ('GLMZ — the biggest stretch of gray-zone machinery in the northern hemisphere, ten times Detroit's machine density' is a clean gloss, but 'CorpoNation-adjacent,' 'CorpoNation registry node,' and 'Φ' amounts appear dozens of times with no first-touch anchoring at all, relying on context alone).
checks.Fix: Give 'CorpoNations' and the Φ currency one brief in-voice orienting beat at their true first mention (e.g., a passing thought like 'a CorpoNation name — the kind of backing that bought silence from ArcSec' or noting Φ as 'the going gray-zone scrip' when she first counts it) rather than letting readers infer their meaning purely from repeated exposure.

checks.Title: Never an acronym before its term
checks.Evidence: 'GLMZ' is used repeatedly throughout (e.g., 'She'd been planning the move for a year... GLMZ — the biggest stretch of gray-zone machinery in the northern hemisphere') without ever giving its full expanded term; similarly 'ArcSec' appears ('A Scalpel crew didn't live this far outside its own territory... ArcSec didn't keep that quiet') with no expansion at first use, and 'CorpoNation' is treated as a known compound term without explanation.
checks.Fix: Introduce GLMZ (and ArcSec) with an in-voice full-term gloss at first mention, e.g., 'the Great Lakes Machine Zone—GLMZ, everyone called it,' before ever using the bare acronym.

checks.Title: Give the POV character one human crack
checks.Evidence: The eigenlift-block moment — 'She had not expected to feel anything about that. She was wrong. Something settled in behind her sternum, warm and level and entirely uninvited, and she left it alone' — and the boots detail where she realizes she stopped padding the toes without noticing, both crack her armor briefly before she re-seals it ('She looked at that a moment... She leaned down and laced them tighter, and left them the way they were').

checks.Title: Land one beat past the handoff
checks.Evidence: The plot business (skim resolved, mother's instruments recovered, boots no longer needing paper) resolves fully, and the final beat—introducing herself as 'Pixel' to Kyle—reads as a hopeful, forward-looking capstone ('A pleasure to meet you') rather than a beat that adds cost or weight; it closes the arc neatly instead of leaving an unresolved pull.
checks.Fix: End one beat earlier or add a final quiet image that carries unresolved cost (e.g., a glance back at 2D's unexplained blood, or the unclosed question of who's really behind that door) instead of landing on the warm, settled note of a new name given freely.

checks.Title: Reward re-reading without requiring it
checks.Evidence: The boots-and-paper detail (padded every morning, then quietly unpadded without her noticing when it changed) works as a complete emotional beat on first read, but a returning reader who knows the ending — her choosing 'Pixel' and stepping into a new identity — will recognize it retroactively as the story's real thesis stated early and physically: she outgrew the old inheritance without marking the moment. Similarly, the AI-warmth motif ('it seemed glad to have been noticed') reads as flavor on a first pass but becomes a thematic rhyme with her own choice to let 2D's door stay closed and to open herself to Kyle, once a reader has the whole arc.

checks.Title: Elevate, don't reconstruct
checks.Evidence: The prose reads as a fully self-contained heist/thriller arc (job, betrayal, investigation, confrontation, resolution) that explains its own terms as it goes—'ghosting,' 'Blur,' 'Husk,' eigenlift suppression fields, the neuretics-generated train—through concrete sensory demonstration rather than lore-dump, which is exactly the 'add doors, don't rebuild the house' move a gateway pass should make.

checks.Title: Orient through GLMZ's five pillars
checks.Evidence: Nanites (used implicitly via 'suppression fields'/eigenlift, matter-shaping repairs, and body infrastructure), Schism, and gray-zone/CorpoNation power are all richly textured, and AIs-as-agents is strongly present (the scheduler, the Pivot AI, the coordination node all 'want' to be asked right and respond with warmth). But neuretics are shown mainly as the protagonist's personal tool for hacking/riding the Pulse illusion, never framed as a social/economic divide between haves and have-nots; and the Schism itself is never named or referenced at all — the eigenlift/suppression-field tech reads as advanced engineering rather than a physics-breaking rift in reality.
checks.Fix: Add a beat that names the Schism explicitly as the origin of the physics-defying eigenlift/suppression tech, and include at least one line marking neuretics as a costly augmentation that divides those who can afford the edge from those who can't (e.g., a client or rival who lacks them and is visibly outmatched because of it).
